newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FISCHER OPENS TRADE AND INVESTMENT CONFERENCE
Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister, Tim Fischer, says the National Trade and Investment Conference opened this morning is about turning contacts into contracts
More than a thousand people from seven international markets are expected to attend the fourth annual conference, at Melbourne's World Congress Centre.
In his opening address, Mr Fischer stressed that the goods and services Australia has on offer meet the needs of developing countries in Asia.
He said Australia is helping these countries to innovate and Australian companies big and small are increasingly finding a market in the region.
MAJORITY IN FAVOUR OF REPUBLIC - POLL
A National Party MP says former Prime Minister Paul Keating's retirement from politics may be partly responsible for a leap in support for Australia becoming a republic.
A Herald AGB McNair poll shows all states except Tasmania now have a majority in favour of a republic.
National MP, Michael Cobb, says Mr Keating's support for a republic may have put people who disliked him off the issue.
Mr Cobb says it will be interesting to see if the support continues in the next two or three polls.
Federal Labor MPs have welcomed the poll's findings.
Labor frontbencher, Daryl Melham, says support for a republic will keep growing, despite the Prime Minister's fondness for the monarchy.
PORT ARTHUR CAFE COMING DOWN
The cafe where 20 people died during the Port Arthur massacre is being demolished.
Work has begun on pulling down the mainly weatherboard rear of the Broad Arrow Cafe.
A spokesman for the authority which manages the historic site, Tim Gardner, says the demolition work is expected to take up to three weeks.
The stonework will be left to be incorporated in a memorial that'll be completed by April 1998, the second anniversary of the massacre.
KENNETT DENIES EYEING FEDERAL PARLIAMENT
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, says people have to accept that neither he nor News Limited Executive Chairman, Ken Cowley, will become Federal politicians.
Mr Cowley has called for the Howard Government to follow Victoria's example on reform, saying Canberra is moving to slowly on change.
Mr Kennett says the Federal Government has already made major advances in industrial refrom and in trying to privatise Telstra, though he differs on taxation.
Nick Economou, a lecturer in Politics at Monash University, says Mr Kennett is wise to stick to state politics.
He says it wouldn't be easy to recreate Victorian political culture in the Federal arena.
TRAVELLERS WARNED AFTER DEATH IN TERRITORY
Police have warned travellers in the Northern Territory to carry water after the death of a man stranded in hot conditions on a remote Territory road.
Police say two men were driving on the Roper Bar Road near Boroloola, toward Cape Crawford on Saturday when their four wheel drive ran out of fuel.
The men stayed with their vehicle, but while resting on the roof, one of them died.
Boroloola Sergeant Keith Currie says the surviving man had no water when he was found yesterday morning, and is lucky to be alive.
POLICE COMMISSION INVESTIGATES JUDGE
The New South Wales Police Royal Commission has revealed that it's been secretly investigating the late supreme court judge David Yeldham for the last 12-months.

The commission has opened a new public segment of its paedophile inquiry, focusing on what a commission lawyer says will be questions about the use of false police documents to either protect or prejudice the late judge.
Mr Yeldham's name was raised in state parliament in relation to questions about alleged preferential treatment given him by the Police Royal Commission.
He commited suicide a month ago.
BEAZLEY BACKS CALLS FOR INTEREST RATE CUT
Federal Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says the Reserve Bank should immediately cut interest rates by another half a per cent.

The Reserve Bank board holds it's monthly meeting today, having announced a rate cut of half-of-one per cent last month. Mr Beazley says the economy is basically strong and there was need for the Reserve Bank to give it a bit of a punch along last month.
But he says a one per cent cut was needed and he hopes the Bank can see it's way clear to correct that.
MELBOURNE TO BECOME A SAFER PLACE
A group of city hotels and nightclubs have signed an historic agreement aimed at making Melbourne's nightlife safer.
Supported by the City of Melbourne, the new Safe City Accord commits members to providing high standards of security and service at their venues.
This includes a focus on the responsible service of alcohol and the promotion of low alcohol and non-alcoholic drinks.
Launching the accord, Police Minister Bill McGrath said it was a vital step towards improving Melbourne's image.
